Everyone remembers Versailles and Trianon. Far fewer remember Neuilly, the 1919 treaty that cut Bulgaria off from the Aegean Sea.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ The Treaty of Neuilly-sur-Seine was signed on 27 November 1919 in the town hall of Neuilly, just west of Paris. Bulgaria had joined the Central Powers in WWI, and this was its bill.
2/ The biggest loss is the red strip in the south: Western Thrace. It went to the Allies, who awarded it to Greece at the San Remo conference. Bulgaria lost its direct outlet to the Aegean.

3/ In the west, Bulgaria handed about 2,563 km² to the new Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes. Bulgarians call these the Western Outlands: areas around Tsaribrod (now Dimitrovgrad), Bosilegrad and Strumica.

4/ Why those strips? The old border ran along high mountain ridges. The new one gave the heights to Belgrade and left Sofia badly exposed. It was also framed as payback for Bulgaria's occupation of Serbia in 1915-18.
5/ The land on this map wasn't all. Bulgaria also had to give Southern Dobruja back to Romania, cut its army to 20,000 men and pay £100 million in reparations.

6/ In Bulgaria, Neuilly is remembered as the Second National Catastrophe. Southern Dobruja came back in 1940 through the Treaty of Craiova. Most of the rest was reoccupied in WWII, but only temporarily.
Harsh punishment or fair price for 1915? Where do you stand on Neuilly? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
